items.title: Today's lesson
items.content:
A car-advert puzzle opens **acceleration**.

One bus trip then carries the whole lesson: we find its acceleration, then draw the same trip as a position–time graph and a velocity–time graph.

Slope and area keep giving back answers you already found.

items.title: You already know
items.content:
• average velocity = displacement ÷ time

• converting km/h into m/s

• reading coordinates off a graph

• area of a rectangle and a triangle

items.title: By the end, you can
items.content:
**1.** Define acceleration, give its SI unit and read its sign.

**2.** Plot and read position–time graphs (slope = velocity).

**3.** Plot and read velocity–time graphs (slope = acceleration, area = displacement).

**4.** Solve graph-based questions.

script.x: ONLY for you, not meant for students.

items.text:
**What this shows**

• Two car adverts. Both cars reach **100 km/h**.

• The sports car does it in **4 seconds**; the family car takes **12 seconds**.

**Answer to Question 1**

It gets to 100 km/h **much faster** — 4 s against 12 s.

**Answer to Question 2**

The **scooter's**. The bus is fast, but its velocity is not changing.

**Answer to Question 3**

When it **starts and stops** — that is, when its velocity changes.

script.x: Show the two adverts. Pointer 1 sets up what they claim.
Questions 1, 2 and 3 in order. Answers are on pointers 2, 3 and 4.
Draw the thread out: Q1 advertised how fast the velocity changes, Q2 picked out which velocity is changing, Q3 noticed the effect.
Show the conclusion box.

items.text:
**What this shows**

• A bus on a straight road, with its speedometer at four moments.

• Leaves **Stop 1** at $t=0$, reads **36 km/h** at $t=10$ s, cruises to $t=30$ s, brakes and stops at **Stop 2** at $t=35$ s.

• Take the direction of motion as **positive**.

**Answer to Question 4**

$36 \times \dfrac{5}{18} = 10\ \text{m/s}$

**Answer to Question 5**

From $0$ to $10\ \text{m/s}$ — a change of $10\ \text{m/s}$.

**Answer to Question 6**

$\dfrac{10}{10} = 1\ \text{m/s}$ every second.

script.x: Show the bus trip. Pointer 1 sets up the four moments.
Questions 4, 5 and 6 in order. Answers are on pointers 2, 3 and 4.
Show the key idea box and write the formula out with them.
Show the conclusion box.

items.text:
**What this shows**

• A bus on a straight road, with its speedometer at four moments.

• Leaves **Stop 1** at $t=0$, reads **36 km/h** at $t=10$ s, cruises to $t=30$ s, brakes and stops at **Stop 2** at $t=35$ s.

• Take the direction of motion as **positive**.

**Answer to Question 7**

**Zero.** The velocity does not change, however fast the bus is going.

**Answer to Question 8**

$a=\dfrac{0-10}{5} = -2\ \text{m/s}^2$

**Answer to Question 9**

The acceleration points **opposite** to the motion, so the bus is **slowing down**.

**What this shows**

• Two cars, both moving in the **+ direction**.

• Speeding up: the acceleration arrow points the **same way** as velocity.

• Slowing down: it points the **opposite** way.

items.prompt: The SI unit of acceleration is
A scooter speeds up from 18 km/h to 36 km/h in 5 s. Its acceleration is

items.text:
**On Question 2**

$u = 18\times\dfrac{5}{18}=5\ \text{m/s}$ and $v = 36\times\dfrac{5}{18}=10\ \text{m/s}$, so $a=\dfrac{10-5}{5}=1\ \text{m/s}^2$, in the direction of motion.

Pointer 1 carries the working for Question 2.

items.prompt: Assertion (A): A train running at a steady 100 km/h on a straight track has zero acceleration.  Reason (R): Acceleration depends on how quickly the velocity changes, not on how large it is.
options: Both A and R are true, and R explains A
Both are true, but R does not explain A
A is true, R is false
A is false, R is true

items.prompt: A stone is dropped from a building. Its velocity is 0, 9.8, 19.6 and 29.4 m/s at t = 0, 1, 2 and 3 s. Its acceleration is
options: 9.8 m/s², and the acceleration is uniform
9.8 m/s², but the acceleration is not uniform
19.6 m/s², and the acceleration is uniform

items.text:
**On Question 2**

The velocity goes up by the same $9.8\ \text{m/s}$  each second, so the acceleration is uniform. This is the acceleration due to gravity, $g = 9.8\ \text{m/s}^2$, downwards.

items.text:
**What this shows**

• The bus's **position**, measured from Stop 1, while it cruises.

• Readings every 5 s, from $t=10$ s to $t=30$ s.

script.x: Show the table. Pointer 1 says what the numbers are.

items.text:
**What this shows**

• The same readings plotted: time across, position up.

• A and B are two points on the line; C completes the triangle ABC.

• BC is the change in position, AC the change in time.

**Answer to Question 10**

A **straight line**.

**Answer to Question 11**

$50\ \text{m}$ each time — equal distances in equal intervals, so **uniform motion**.

script.x: Show the plotted graph. Pointer 1 sets it up.
Questions 10 and 11. Answers are on pointers 2 and 3.

items.text:
**What this shows**

• The same readings plotted: time across, position up.

• A and B are two points on the line; C completes the triangle ABC.

• BC is the change in position, AC the change in time.

**Answer to Question 12**

$BC = 200-100 = 100\ \text{m}$;  $AC = 25-15 = 10\ \text{s}$.

**Answer to Question 13**

$\dfrac{100\ \text{m}}{10\ \text{s}} = 10\ \text{m/s}$ — change in position ÷ time, which is the **velocity**.

**Answer to Question 14**

**Yes.** $10\ \text{m/s} = 36\ \text{km/h}$.

**Answer to Question 16**

**Constant velocity**, $10\ \text{m/s}$.

items.prompt: The position–time graphs of two objects A and B are shown. Which one has the greater velocity?

items.text:
**On this question**

B's line is **steeper**, so it covers more displacement in the same time.

items.prompt: The graph shows Meera's walk along a straight corridor. Her velocity from O to A, what she does from A to B, and her velocity from B to C are

items.text:
**On this question**

$\dfrac{12}{4}=3\ \text{m/s}$ from O to A; flat from A to B, so at rest at $12\ \text{m}$; $\dfrac{0-12}{4}=-3\ \text{m/s}$ from B to C — she walks back.

items.text:
**What this shows**

• The **same** bus trip, now with **velocity** up the Y-axis.

• O to P pulling away, P to Q cruising at $10\ \text{m/s}$, Q to R braking, R to S waiting.

**Answer to Question 19**

**No.** It moves at a **constant velocity** of $10\ \text{m/s}$.

**Answer to Question 20**

From **R to S**, where the line lies **on** the time axis: $v=0$.

items.text:
**What this shows**

• The **same** bus trip, now with **velocity** up the Y-axis.

• O to P pulling away, P to Q cruising at $10\ \text{m/s}$, Q to R braking, R to S waiting.

**Answer to Question 21**

$\dfrac{10}{10} = 1\ \text{m/s}^2$ — the acceleration we found in Part 1.

**Answer to Question 22**

$\dfrac{0-10}{5} = -2\ \text{m/s}^2$ — the braking.

items.text:
**What this shows**

• The same graph, with the region under the line split into three parts.

• **1** and **3** are triangles; **2** is a rectangle.

**Answer to Question 23**

$10\ \text{m/s} \times 20\ \text{s} = 200\ \text{m}$.

**Answer to Question 24**

The **area of rectangle 2**: $20\ \text{s} \times 10\ \text{m/s} = 200\ \text{m}$. Its unit, (m/s) × s, is metres.

script.x: Show the shaded graph. Pointer 1 names the three parts.
Questions 23 and 24. Answers are on pointers 2 and 3.

items.text:
**What this shows**

• The same graph, with the region under the line split into three parts.

• **1** and **3** are triangles; **2** is a rectangle.

**Answer to Question 25**

$\tfrac{1}{2}\times 10\times 10 = 50\ \text{m}$ and $\tfrac{1}{2}\times 5\times 10 = 25\ \text{m}$.

**Answer to Question 26**

$50+200+25 = 275\ \text{m}$ — the **same** value the bus stopped at on the position–time graph.

items.prompt: The velocity–time graph of a car is a straight line parallel to the time axis at 15 m/s. The car is
Assertion (A): Two cars whose velocity–time graphs are parallel straight lines have equal accelerations.  Reason (R): The slope of a velocity–time graph gives the acceleration.
options: Both A and R are true, and R explains A
Both are true, but R does not explain A
A is true, R is false
A is false, R is true

items.text:
**On Question 2**

Parallel lines have **equal slopes**, so the accelerations are equal.

items.prompt: For the graph shown, the acceleration between A and B, and the displacement between 10 s and 20 s, are

items.text:
**On this question**

$a=\dfrac{10-5}{20-10}=0.5\ \text{m/s}^2$.

Displacement = rectangle $(10\times 5 = 50)$ + triangle $(\tfrac{1}{2}\times 10\times 5 = 25)$ = $75\ \text{m}$.
